transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I’m here because I keep running into this wall with work that takes a lot of sitting down and thinking. Things like monthly reports or planning a multi-site health event—I know they’re important, but I put them off and have a really hard time getting myself to start or stay with them.
Did you have similar trouble starting or sticking with tasks when you were a child?

Yes, I did. Even back in elementary school, teachers would tell my parents I was bright, but I was always daydreaming. I’d lose worksheets or forget to turn in homework, and my mom pretty much had to check my backpack every night or it just wouldn’t get done or handed in.
Do you have this same trouble focusing and following through in other parts of your life besides work?

Yes. It shows up outside of work too. I’m still getting by, but it’s not like it doesn’t cost anything. People end up covering gaps for me sometimes, deadlines slip, and then I’m the one making last-minute apologies to coworkers or friends. It’s embarrassing, honestly.
Do these same focus and follow-through problems happen at home too?

Yes, they do. At home and with community stuff, I’ll forget to return calls from volunteers or miss small errands I said I’d do for an event. A couple times, I’ve even had a community meeting completely slip my mind until someone texted me, and then I had to apologize. It’s frustrating because it’s usually not that I don’t care—it just drops out of my head.
Do you often feel restless or fidgety?
Not really, no. I mean, I might shift around a bit if I’m bored or sitting too long, but I wouldn’t say I’m usually restless or fidgety.
